subject: Choosing cabinet finishes and handles
hook: Top of the base door, bottom of the wall door: handle placement explained.
ig:
Top of the base door, bottom of the wall door: handle placement explained.

Handle style gets all the attention. Handle position decides whether the kitchen is comfortable to use.

The principle is simple: put the handle where your hand naturally is.

Base units: near the top edge. You open them without stooping.
Wall units: near the bottom edge, so shorter members of the family can reach.
Tall larders and housings: roughly at worktop height, which keeps a line through the kitchen.
Drawers: centred, so they pull straight and run smoothly.

Keep handles aligned across the run, too. When bar handles line up from door to door, the whole kitchen looks calmer, whichever finish you chose.

It is the kind of detail we sort out on your design before anything is made, rather than with a drill on fitting day.

Which handles have you got at home, and do they sit in the right place? Tell us below.
fb:
A detail you only notice when it is wrong: where the handles sit on your kitchen doors.

The rule we design to is handles where your hand naturally is. Near the top of base units, near the bottom of wall units, around worktop height on tall larders, and centred on drawers. Lined up across the run, they make the whole kitchen look calmer.
